intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Montgomery County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: The results of our tests disclosed no instances of noncompliance or other matters that are required to be reported under Government Auditing Standards.
verdicts.detail: On internal control, the auditors wrote: “During our audit we did not identify any deficiencies in internal control that we consider to be material weaknesses.”

limits: From the 2024 report, dated June 17, 2026. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.

cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the offices of Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer. Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer The Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer received more salary payments and health insurance reimbursements than they were entitled to during the period January 1, 2024 through May 31, 2025, resulting in overpayments totaling $108,684 as follows: Mayor ($94,491) • 26 extra payroll checks totaling $74,211. • 36 extra health insurance reimbursement checks totaling $20,280. As of May 31, 2025, the Mayor had been paid $31,121 of the authorized 2025 yearly salary of $34,799.
